questions.question: What is the key distinction between a workflow and an agent in Anthropic's framing?
options: Workflows use GPT-4 and agents use Claude
Workflows have predefined code-owned paths; agents have model-owned dynamic paths
Workflows are for production; agents are only for research
Workflows use one LLM call; agents use multiple
questions.explanation: In Anthropic's framing, workflows are LLMs and tools orchestrated through predefined code paths (engineer-owned graph) while agents dynamically direct their own tools and take their own steps (model-owned graph).

questions.question: What are Anthropic's five workflow patterns?
options: Plan, Execute, Verify, Review, Handoff
Prompt chaining, Routing, Parallelization, Orchestrator-workers, Evaluator-optimizer
Retrieval, Generation, Evaluation, Refinement, Output
Input, Process, Validate, Output, Log
questions.explanation: Anthropic's five workflow patterns (Schluntz and Zhang, Dec 2024): prompt chaining, routing, parallelization (sectioning and voting), orchestrator-workers, and evaluator-optimizer.

questions.question: What is the 'parallelization' workflow pattern, and what are its two shapes?
options: Running the same agent on multiple machines; shapes: horizontal and vertical scaling
Running N LLM calls concurrently and aggregating; shapes: sectioning (different chunks) and voting (same prompt, N runs)
Running multiple tools in parallel; shapes: dependent and independent
Running a pipeline in parallel stages; shapes: map and reduce
questions.explanation: Parallelization runs N LLM calls concurrently and aggregates results. Sectioning splits different chunks of work across calls; voting runs the same prompt N times and takes a majority or synthesized result.

questions.question: When should you prefer a workflow over an agent?
options: When the task is open-ended research with unknown next steps
When steps are predictable, cost is constrained, or compliance requires an auditable graph
When the task takes more than an hour to complete
When the task involves multiple modalities
questions.explanation: Workflows beat agents when tasks are predictable (steps can be enumerated), cost-bound (workflows have bounded step counts), or compliance-bound (auditors need to read the graph, not infer it from trajectories).

questions.question: What is the 'augmented LLM' concept that underlies all five patterns?
options: An LLM with a larger context window
One LLM with three capabilities wired in: search (retrieval), tools (actions), and memory (persistence)
An LLM that has been fine-tuned on tool use
Multiple LLMs working together
questions.explanation: The augmented LLM is the atomic unit: one LLM with search (retrieval), tools (actions), and memory (persistence) wired in. All five workflow patterns combine augmented LLMs in different topologies.

questions.question: What is the evaluator-optimizer workflow pattern?
options: An optimizer that automatically tunes LLM hyperparameters
One LLM proposes an answer, another evaluates and produces a critique, iterate until the evaluator passes
A pipeline that optimizes prompt length automatically
A system that routes queries to the best model
questions.explanation: The evaluator-optimizer pattern has two roles: one LLM proposes an output, another evaluates it and produces a critique. The loop iterates until the evaluator passes. This is Self-Refine (Lesson 05) generalized and named in Anthropic's workflow vocabulary.
